correctness.rationale: The span of Hermitian hopping eigenvectors vanishing on the sinks reduces both hopping and loss. On its orthogonal complement, taking the imaginary part of each lossy eigenvalue's Rayleigh quotient forces strictly negative imaginary part, since equality would force the eigenvector into that dark span. The finite-dimensional complementary semigroup therefore tends to zero, including in the presence of Jordan blocks. In the Bloch basis, degeneracy requires 2Φ=0 modulo 2π; a simple mode cannot vanish at a sink. In a doublet there is just one line of candidates, with a sine envelope around the first sink and divisibility condition N | (2k−p)(t−a). At zero flux this gives h frequencies before identifying opposite signs and deleting self-pairs. At half flux the solvability condition is N/g odd, and the g odd-frequency representatives give floor(g/2) doublets after deleting the possible unpaired zero-sine representative. Summing squared site amplitudes by the finite geometric-series identity gives the stated zero-flux profile and the enhanced half-flux survival at the even-g antipode. For the thresholds, each dark edge needs an effective congruence (odd p | N or mod 2 if 4 | N at zero flux). A shared congruence on two edges darkens the triple; three distinct congruences suffice by assigning a different equal pair in each modulus by CRT. At half flux an even cycle already forces every dark pair into the same full 2-power residue class, making the whole triple dark. For odd N both flux tests coincide. The least admissible sizes are 4·3·5=60 and 3·5·7=105; direct gcds give pair dimensions (2,4,1) and (1,2,3) at the respective claimed fluxes, with no collective dark state.
